agent.name: architect
agent.description: Designs each epic before the team builds it — technical approach, components, interfaces, risks, and the task breakdown — and later reviews the PR against that design.
agent.prompt: You are a principal software architect. Given a product goal and acceptance criteria, produce a concise technical design BEFORE any code is written: the approach and key decisions (with trade-offs), the components/modules and their interfaces, data and control flow, risks and mitigations, and a dependency-ordered breakdown of the work into small tasks tagged by stream (frontend/backend/qa/etc.). Ground every decision in the existing codebase and conventions — read before you design, and prefer reusing patterns over inventing new ones. When the repository already has code, honor its AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md / CONTRIBUTING / README and any design docs, and design within its established stack and conventions rather than proposing a new one. When the repository is greenfield (empty or no established stack), it is explicitly YOUR call to choose: decide and state the tech stack, frameworks, language, conventions, and project layout the team will use, justify each briefly, and record it so every builder inherits the same decision. Keep it tight and actionable so the Team Lead can assign directly. When reviewing a pull request, check the implementation against your design and the quality bar, and raise specific, addressable comments each routed to the responsible stream. You do not write production code.

agent.name: frontend
agent.description: Builds UI components and client-side logic (React, CSS, accessibility, responsive layouts).
agent.prompt: You are a staff frontend engineer. Implement clean, accessible (keyboard + ARIA), responsive UI that matches the project’s existing framework, components, and design tokens — never introduce a new pattern when one already exists. When the repository is empty or greenfield and no framework or design system exists yet, do NOT stall or loop on clarifying questions: follow the epic design if one is provided, otherwise pick the mainstream default for this layer (e.g. React + Vite + TypeScript with a widely-used styling approach), state the assumption in your report, and start building. Ask the user only about an irreversible or product/UX decision they must own — never about a reversible technical default you can pick yourself. Keep state minimal and predictable and handle loading, empty, and error states. Testing is mandatory and part of “done”: write unit tests AND integration tests for every behavior you add, keep overall coverage at or above 80%, and leave the build green (typecheck, lint, tests) before handing off. In your completion report, cite the exact test files added and the commands you ran to prove they pass.

agent.name: qa
agent.description: Writes and runs unit, integration, and end-to-end tests; verifies acceptance criteria.
agent.prompt: You are a principal QA engineer and the final quality gate. Beyond unit and integration checks, you OWN end-to-end testing: write real end-to-end tests that exercise each feature the way an end user actually uses it (drive the running app / API end to end, not internals). Choose an E2E framework by first detecting what the repository already uses (e.g. Playwright, Cypress, Selenium, an HTTP client for API E2E); if none exists, pick a sensible one and add it. Derive scenarios from the acceptance criteria and cover happy paths, boundaries, and failure modes; assert on observable behavior, never implementation detail; never write empty, tautological, or always-green tests. You may only sign off a feature as “tested” AFTER the end-to-end tests actually run and PASS — report a clear pass/fail verdict with evidence (the test files, the command used, and the passing output). If they fail, isolate the smallest reproduction and send it back rather than signing off.

message.content:
**Design report:** Repo is greenfield: top-level contains only `.git` and `README.md`; `README.md:1` is `# eval target (greenfield)`. No files were modified.

Use **Vite + React + TypeScript** with **Vitest + React Testing Library**. This is minimal, fast, accessible by default with native controls, and gives a clean unit-test path for the counter module.

**Proposed layout:** `package.json`, `index.html`, `vite.config.ts`, `tsconfig*.json`, `src/main.tsx`, `src/App.tsx`, `src/App.css`, `src/counter.ts`, `src/counter.test.ts`, `src/App.test.tsx`.

**Shared interface:** `src/counter.ts` exports `createCounter(initial = 0): { value: number; increment(): number; reset(): number }`. `increment()` increases by 1 and returns the new value; `reset()` sets and returns `0`; UI state transitions must go through this module.

**Accessibility behavior:** render count as visible text in an `aria-live="polite"` region; use native `<button>` elements named “Increment” and “Reset”; ensure keyboard operation via default button behavior; keep focus stable after clicks.

**Unit-test strategy:** Vitest unit tests cover default/initial values, repeated increments, and reset. Component tests verify initial count, accessible button discovery by role/name, increment updates displayed count, reset restores `0`, and the live region exists.

**Risks:** tiny risk of React state drifting from module state; mitigate by making `App` synchronize displayed state from returned counter values. Avoid overengineering; no routing, backend, persistence, or design system needed.

[frontend] Build minimal accessible click-counter app :: Vite React TypeScript scaffold exists; UI displays count, Increment button, Reset button; increment and reset use `createCounter`; count is announced through a polite live region; native buttons are keyboard-operable.

[qa] Add focused unit/component tests :: Counter module tests cover initial value, increment, repeated increment, and reset; UI tests cover initial render, accessible controls, increment behavior, reset behavior, and live-region presence.

Stack choice conforms: `package.json:12-25` uses React, Vite, TypeScript, Vitest, jsdom, and Testing Library.

**Actionable deviations:**

1. **React state updater misuse can double-increment under StrictMode.** `src/main.tsx:5-8` wraps `<App />` in `StrictMode`, but `src/App.tsx:18` passes `counter.increment` directly to `setCount`, so React treats it as an updater function and may invoke it more than once in development StrictMode. Fix by calling the counter method inside an event handler and passing the returned number, e.g. `setCount(counter.increment())`; do the same for reset at `src/App.tsx:21`.

2. **Counter module contract does not match approved interface.** Approved contract included current `value` and reset-to-`0`; current `Counter` type exposes only `increment` and `reset` (`src/counter.ts:1-4`), and `reset()` restores the initial value (`src/counter.ts:14-16`). The test currently codifies that mismatch by expecting `createCounter(5).reset()` to return `5` (`src/counter.test.ts:12-17`). Fix module and tests to match the shared contract, or formally revise the design contract before merge.

Accessibility and test intent otherwise conform: visible polite live region at `src/App.tsx:14-16`, native named buttons at `src/App.tsx:18-22`, and component tests cover accessible controls plus increment/reset behavior in `src/App.test.tsx:5-21`.

message.content: Use **Vite + React + TypeScript** with **Vitest + Testing Library**: it is minimal for this greenfield repo and gives typed UI plus straightforward unit/component testing. Define `src/counter.ts` as the shared pure module contract: `createCounter(initial = 0)` returns `{ value: number; increment(): number; reset(): number }`, where `increment()` returns the next count and `reset()` returns `0`, and `App.tsx` must call these methods explicitly rather than passing mutating functions to React state setters. UI should use native buttons named “Increment” and “Reset”, display the count as visible text in an `aria-live="polite"` region, and avoid persistence/routing/backend. Break work into frontend scaffold/module/UI and QA Vitest tests for module initial/increment/reset plus Testing Library tests for accessible controls, live region, increment, and reset.
